tasks.title: packaging: the Linux x64 platform package and the launcher shim

details.goal: npm i -g sangkar-mcp must install a native binary on Linux x64 with no Bun and no build step, and must refuse every other platform by name instead of failing obscurely.
details.contract:
The first Rust release targets ONE platform: `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`.
`package.json`: keep the name `sangkar-mcp` and the current version; `bin` becomes `{"sangkar": "bin/sangkar.js"}`; `files` becomes `["bin", "agent", "README.md"]`; `optionalDependencies` declares exactly one entry, `sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu`, pinned to the SAME version as the parent; `engines` becomes `{"node": ">=18"}` (the shim only — the server is native); remove every `scripts` entry that invokes bun/tsc/biome/drizzle.
`bin/sangkar.js`: `#!/usr/bin/env node`, CommonJS, no dependencies. It resolves a platform key from `process.platform` + `process.arch` and needs exactly one mapping for now (`linux:x64` -> `sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu`). If the key is not that one, or the package is not installed, it prints ONE stderr line and exits 70, naming: the key it wanted, the single published platform, and the version to pin to stay on the TypeScript build (`sangkar-mcp@<the current beta line>`). Otherwise it `spawnSync`s `<pkg>/bin/sangkar` with `stdio: 'inherit'`, forwarding every argv byte, and exits with the child's code. Forward SIGINT/SIGTERM to the child.
The key table is DATA (one map plus one refusal string) so adding macOS or Windows later is one entry, one `npm/<key>/` directory and one release-matrix row — never a rewrite.
`rust/scripts/package.sh`: `cargo build --release --locked -p sangkar-cli --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `strip`, then lay out `npm/linux-x64-gnu/bin/sangkar` and `npm/linux-x64-gnu/package.json` with `{"name", "version", "os": ["linux"], "cpu": ["x64"], "files": ["bin"], "license": "MIT", "repository"}` consistent with the parent.
`npm/` holds the generated layout, committed as a template for the release workflow (the workflow fills the version).
Verify on this machine only (Linux x64): `node bin/sangkar.js status --repo-root rust/tests/parity/fixtures/polyglot --data-dir <temp>` answers, and moving `node_modules/sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu` aside makes the shim exit 70 with the one-line refusal.
steps: Rewrite package.json (name/version kept, bin, files, ONE optionalDependency, engines, scripts pruned).
Write bin/sangkar.js with the one-entry key table, the refusal line and signal forwarding.
Write rust/scripts/package.sh for the single target and generate npm/linux-x64-gnu/.
Build, run the shim against a fixture, then rename the platform package aside and record the refusal.
details.verify:
`node bin/sangkar.js --help` exits 0 and prints the same usage the native binary prints.
`node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./package.json').optionalDependencies).join())"` prints exactly `sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu`.
Done when: moving the platform package aside makes the shim exit 70 with one stderr line naming the wanted key, the published platform and the version to pin.

tasks.title: CI and release: one target, artifacts, no npm publish

details.goal: Every push checks formatting, lints and tests on the pinned toolchain; a tag builds the single Linux x64 binary and attaches it, leaving the npm publish to the maintainer (it needs an OTP).
details.contract:
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`: on push/PR — `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` on `ubuntu-latest` with `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.100.0` and a `Swatinem/rust-cache` step. `git` must be available for the diff tests. One job only: a macOS job lands with the macOS release (open question 3 is answered "Linux x64 first"), and adding it later must be an extension of this file, not a rewrite.
`.github/workflows/release.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` plus `push: tags: ['v*']`; ONE target, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, built on `ubuntu-22.04` because that image decides the glibc floor (2.35) — record the floor in a comment and in the release notes; `cargo build --release --locked`; run `rust/scripts/package.sh`; upload the platform package as an artifact; create a GitHub Release on a tag and attach the tarball plus the platform `.tgz`. Do NOT run `npm publish` in CI — the release notes say the maintainer publishes TWO packages by hand in order (the platform package first, then the parent), matching `.agents/skills/build-n-deploy`.
Keep both files minimal: no matrix of Rust versions, no `cargo-audit`, no cache keys that expire silently.
steps: Write ci.yml with the single ubuntu job and the pinned toolchain.
Write release.yml with the one target, the glibc comment and the artifact upload.
Add the step that creates the GitHub Release on a tag.
Add the note that npm publish is manual, in which order, and why the platform package goes first.
details.verify:
`python3 -c "import yaml; [yaml.safe_load(open(p)) for p in ['.github/workflows/ci.yml','.github/workflows/release.yml']]"` parses both files (install-free check).
Done when: the release workflow names exactly one target, records the glibc floor, and contains no `npm publish`.

tasks.title: Move the SQL into the crate and repoint both readers

details.goal: End the two-copy risk: the migrations live inside the crate that owns them, and the TypeScript reader is repointed at the new location for the short time it still exists.
details.contract:
`git mv src/shared/store/migrations rust/crates/sangkar-store/migrations` preserving BYTES for `0000_init.sql`, `raw/0001_fts.sql` and `meta/` (the drizzle journal is kept as history). `migrations.rs`'s two `include_str!` paths become `../migrations/0000_init.sql` and `../migrations/raw/0001_fts.sql`; add a compile-time assertion that `schema_version() == 2`.
`src/shared/store/migrate.ts`'s `MIGRATIONS_DIR` is repointed with a comment saying it is the pre-cutover stopgap and is deleted in TASK-063. `bun run db:drift` and `bun test` must stay green — that is the proof the move lost nothing.
Do not regenerate any SQL: `drizzle-kit` is about to be deleted, and a regenerated file would change bytes.
steps: `git mv` the migrations directory into the crate.
Update the two include paths and add the version assertion.
Repoint the TypeScript `MIGRATIONS_DIR` with its stopgap comment.
Run `bun run db:drift` and both test suites.
details.verify:
`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-store --test migrate` exits 0.
`~/.bun/bin/bun run db:drift` exits 0 and `git diff --stat` shows no change under the new migrations path.
Done when: `sha256sum` of both SQL files is unchanged from `3592da3` (record the hashes).

details.goal: The agent-facing text ships inside the binary, byte for byte, with the TypeScript reader repointed until it is deleted.
details.contract:
`git mv src/prompts/INSTRUCTIONS.md rust/crates/sangkar-core/assets/INSTRUCTIONS.md` (bytes preserved); `include_str!("../assets/INSTRUCTIONS.md")`; the byte-count assertion from TASK-025 keeps working unchanged (it must, which is the proof nothing changed).
`src/shared/instructions.ts` reads the file from the new location with the same stopgap comment as TASK-061; `tests/instructions.test.ts` must stay green.
Do not re-word a single sentence, and do not add a trailing newline: the suite pins these bytes.
steps: `git mv` the markdown.
Update the include path and confirm the length assertion still passes.
Repoint the TypeScript reader.
Run both suites.
details.verify:
`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-core --test instructions` exits 0 with the same byte count as before the move.
`~/.bun/bin/bun test tests/instructions.test.ts` exits 0.
Done when: `sha256sum` of the markdown is unchanged from `3592da3`.

details.goal: One implementation, one tree: remove the TypeScript source, its test suite and its lint/schema tooling, keeping only the shim the npm package needs.
details.contract:
Delete `src/`, `tests/`, `bin/sangkar.ts`, `biome.json`, `drizzle.config.ts`. KEEP `bin/sangkar.js` (TASK-058's shim) and KEEP `agent/` (the distributable skill).
Preconditions, checked before deleting: TASK-061/062 have moved every asset the Rust tree embeds, so `grep -rn 'include_str!' rust/crates` names no path under `src/`.
After deleting: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo test -p sangkar-cli --test goldens` must all pass with no TypeScript anywhere — the goldens are now the only oracle, which is the point of having captured them.
Also update `.sangkarignore` if it still names a deleted path, and confirm `git grep -l 'bun:sqlite\|drizzle-orm\|web-tree-sitter\|@toon-format'` returns nothing outside `docs/` and `.ppm/` history.
steps: Run the precondition greps and record their output.
Delete the five paths (keep `bin/sangkar.js`).
Run the full Rust suite plus the golden suite.
Run the four-technology grep and record the remaining hits (docs and plan history only).
details.verify:
`cargo test --workspace` and the golden suite exit 0 with `src/` absent.
`ls src tests 2>&1 | grep -c 'No such file'` prints 2.
Done when: the report lists the four grep results and states the repository test count before and after.

details.goal: The npm package must describe a native binary and nothing else: no Bun engine, no TypeScript toolchain, no drizzle, no import map.
details.contract:
`package.json`: delete `"type": "module"` (the shim is CommonJS, and a `module` type would make Node parse it as ESM), delete the `imports` map (`#shared/*`), delete every `devDependencies` entry, delete the bun-only `scripts` (`test`, `typecheck`, `lint`, `build`, `db:*`, `acceptance`, `index`, `status`, `dev`, `mcp`), keep `release:beta`, keep `bin`/`files`/`optionalDependencies`/`engines.node`/`keywords`/`repository`/`license`, and refresh `description` if it still mentions Bun.
Delete `tsconfig.json`, `bunfig.toml`, `bun.lock`.
`.gitignore`: drop `dist/`-only rules that no longer apply, add `/rust/target/`, keep `.sangkar/`, `.codegraph/`, `*.db*`, `node_modules/`.
After this task `node bin/sangkar.js --help` (the only entry point) still works, and `npm pack --dry-run` lists `bin`, `agent`, `README.md` and nothing TypeScript.
steps: Rewrite package.json by deletion only (no version change).
Delete the three config files and the lockfile.
Update .gitignore for the Rust target directory.
Run `npm pack --dry-run` and `node bin/sangkar.js --help`.
details.verify:
`npm pack --dry-run --json | python3 -c "import json,sys; print([f['path'] for f in json.load(sys.stdin)[0]['files']])"` shows no `.ts` file.
`node bin/sangkar.js --help` exits 0.
Done when: `grep -c '"type"' package.json` prints 0 and the pack list contains `bin/sangkar.js`.

tasks.title: Docs: the product record describes the Rust artifact

details.contract:
`docs/my-product/TECH-SPEC.md` §15: replace the Bun distribution table with the native one — ONE platform package (`sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu`), the Node shim, the glibc floor taken from the release image, the measured binary size (record it, do not estimate), why the shim is Node rather than `sh`, and the exact steps that add a second platform (one `optionalDependencies` row, one `npm/<key>/`, one release-matrix row). Rewrite the 'runtime facts' paragraph: no Bun, no WASM grammars, `rusqlite` bundled, tree-sitter compiled in, and the module-isolation paragraph now points at the crate DAG.
`docs/maintainers.md`: new build/release procedure — `cargo build --release --locked --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `rust/scripts/package.sh`, the TWO-package publish order (platform then parent) with the OTP note, the glibc floor, and the tag format.
`README.md`: keep its fixed shape (`## sangkar-mcp`, `## Installation & Requirements`, `## Usage` with `### MCP & Skill` and `### CLI`, `## License`); `Installation & Requirements` says Linux x64 with the named glibc floor, Node ≥ 18 for the shim only, no Bun; and it states plainly that macOS and Windows stay on the last TypeScript release until their platform ships. Update the version/registry lines that name the current release state.
`.agents/skills/build-n-deploy/SKILL.md`: the SemVer standard and the two-version-string rule stay; the preflight becomes the cargo gates plus the golden suite; the publish step becomes the two packages, platform first.
Do not invent numbers: build the release binary first and use its actual size.
steps: Build the release binary for the target and record its size.
Rewrite TECH-SPEC §15, the runtime facts and the add-a-platform steps.
Rewrite maintainers.md's build/release sections with the two-package order and the glibc floor.
Update README's installation and usage sections in its fixed shape, including the macOS/Windows statement.
Update the release skill's preflight and publish steps.
details.verify:

tasks.title: Docs: the shipped agent skill stops mentioning Bun

details.goal: agent/ ships in the npm tarball and tells an agent how to install and run this server; after cutover it must not tell anyone to run bin/sangkar.ts through Bun.
details.contract:
Three files carry the stale wording: agent/README.md:51 and agent/install.sh:179-180 both say to run `<repo>/bin/sangkar.ts` through `~/.bun/bin/bun` when the CLI is not on PATH, and agent/SKILL.md's YAML frontmatter declares `compatibility: … Bun 1.4.4+.` — that line ships the requirement into every agent that loads the skill. Replace them with the installed binary (`sangkar mcp --repo-root <path>`, or `npx sangkar-mcp mcp --repo-root <path>` when nothing is on PATH) and with a compatibility line that states the truth: `Requires Linux x64 in the first Rust release; Node.js >=18 for the launcher shim only; the server is a native binary with no interpreter.`
agent/SKILL.md restates the seven tool manifests (names, arguments, defaults, budget ceilings) and the install matrix for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi; re-read it against `rust/crates/sangkar-tools/src/*/manifest.rs`, correct any drift, then run every command it quotes.
Do not change argument names, defaults or budget numbers: they are the contract. Only the runtime/install sentences change, plus any drift the manifests reveal.
steps: Grep both stale command lines and the frontmatter requirement, and rewrite all three around the installed binary and npx.
Re-read SKILL.md against the seven manifests and correct drift.
Run install.sh against a temp HOME and confirm it leaves a working MCP config.
Run one quoted MCP snippet end to end.
details.verify:
`grep -rni 'bun' agent/` returns nothing (case-insensitive: the frontmatter spells it `Bun`).
`bash agent/install.sh --help` (or its documented dry-run) exits 0.
Done when: every command quoted in the three files has been executed once and the manifest table matches the Rust manifests field by field.
